papers.title: Correlated Random Measures
papers.abstract: We develop correlated random measures, random measures where the atom weights can exhibit a flexible pattern of dependence, and use them to develop powerful hierarchical Bayesian nonparametric models. Hierarchical Bayesian nonparametric models are usually built from completely random measures, a Poisson-process based construction in which the atom weights are independent. Completely random measures imply strong independence assumptions in the corresponding hierarchical model, and these assumptions are often misplaced in real-world settings. Correlated random measures address this limitation. They model correlation within the measure by using a Gaussian process in concert with the Poisson process. With correlated random measures, for example, we can develop a latent feature model for which we can infer both the properties of the latent features and their dependency pattern. We develop several other examples as well. We study a correlated random measure model of pairwise count data. We derive an efficient variational inference algorithm and show improved predictive performance on large data sets of documents, web clicks, and electronic health records.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文是关于贝叶斯非参数统计方法的，与FEA替代建模或生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on Bayesian nonparametric models for count data and does not address FEA surrogate modeling, expensive simulation sampling, constraints, UQ, or biomechanics/implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决完全随机测度中原子权重独立假设的局限性。
summary_zh.method: 提出相关随机测度，结合高斯过程和泊松过程建模依赖模式。
summary_zh.result: 在文档、点击和电子健康记录数据集上提高了预测性能。
summary_zh.validation: 在三个大规模数据集上验证预测性能。

summary_en.motivation: To overcome the unrealistic independence assumptions in completely random measures used in hierarchical Bayesian nonparametric models.
summary_en.method: Correlated random measures are developed by combining Gaussian processes with Poisson processes to model flexible dependency patterns among atom weights.
summary_en.result: Improved predictive performance on large datasets of documents, web clicks, and electronic health records.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated via variational inference on three real-world large-scale datasets.

papers.title: Electronic Structure and the Properties of Phosphorene Systems
papers.abstract: A single atomic layer of black phosphorus, phosphorene, was experimentally realized in 2014. It has a puckered honeycomb lattice structure and a semiconducting electronic structure. In the first part of this paper, we use a simple LCAO model, and discuss qualitatively the electronic structure of phosphorene systems under electric and magnetic fields, especially, noting their midgap edge states. The next part is spent for the review of the research progress on phosphorene in the past one year since its appearance in 2014. Phosphorene has been a typical object to study the semiconductor physics in atomic layers.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究磷烯的电子结构，与生物医学增材制造及植入物力学性能完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on the electronic structure of a 2D material (phosphorene) and does not address implant design, LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing, or biomedical applications.

summary_en.method: A simple LCAO model was used to qualitatively describe electronic states, combined with a review of recent progress.
summary_en.result: Midgap edge states under electric and magnetic fields were discussed, and the research progress since 2014 was summarized.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; purely theoretical and review-based.

papers.title: Anomaly Detection and Removal Using Non-Stationary Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel Gaussian process approach to fault removal in time-series data. Fault removal does not delete the faulty signal data but, instead, massages the fault from the data. We assume that only one fault occurs at any one time and model the signal by two separate non-parametric Gaussian process models for both the physical phenomenon and the fault. In order to facilitate fault removal we introduce the Markov Region Link kernel for handling non-stationary Gaussian processes. This kernel is piece-wise stationary but guarantees that functions generated by it and their derivatives (when required) are everywhere continuous. We apply this kernel to the removal of drift and bias errors in faulty sensor data and also to the recovery of EOG artifact corrupted EEG signals.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究时间序列异常检测，与用户关注的有限元代理模型或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address surrogate modeling for expensive simulations, does not handle optimization constraints, and does not provide uncertainty quantification for design problems; it focuses on anomaly detection in time-series data.

summary_zh.method: 使用两个独立的高斯过程分别建模物理现象与故障，并引入马尔可夫区域链接核处理非平稳性。

summary_zh.validation: 通过传感器数据和脑电信号实验进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: Propose a novel Gaussian process approach for anomaly removal in time-series data without deleting faulty samples.
summary_en.method: Model the signal with two separate GP components for physical phenomenon and fault, and introduce the Markov Region Link kernel for non-stationary GPs to ensure continuity.
summary_en.result: The method effectively removes drift and bias errors in sensor data and recovers EOG artifact-corrupted EEG signals.
summary_en.validation: Demonstrated on sensor fault datasets and EEG signals with known artifacts.

papers.title: Cell and protein compatible 3D bioprinting of mechanically strong constructs for bone repair
papers.abstract: Rapid prototyping of bone tissue engineering constructs often utilizes elevated temperatures, organic solvents and/or UV light for materials processing. These harsh conditions may prevent the incorporation of cells and therapeutic proteins in the fabrication processes. Here we developed a method for using bioprinting to produce constructs from a thermoresponsive microparticulate material based on poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) at ambient conditions. These constructs could be engineered with yield stresses of up to 1.22 MPa and Young's moduli of up to 57.3 MPa which are within the range of properties of human cancellous bone. Further study showed that protein-releasing microspheres could be incorporated into the bioprinted constructs. The release of the model protein lysozyme from bioprinted constructs was sustainted for a period of 15 days and a high degree of protein activity could be measured up to day 9. This work suggests that bioprinting is a viable route to the production of mechanically strong constructs for bone repair under mild conditions which allow the inclusion of viable cells and active proteins.

papers.title: Shorter, rough trunnion surfaces are associated with higher taper wear rates than longer, smooth trunnion surfaces in a contemporary large head metal‐on‐metal total hip arthroplasty system
papers.abstract: Taper wear at the head-neck junction is a possible cause of early failure in large head metal-on-metal (LH-MoM) hip replacements. We hypothesized that: (i) taper wear may be more pronounced in certain product designs; and (ii) an increased abductor moment arm may be protective. The tapers of 104 explanted LH-MoM hip replacements revised for adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD) from a single manufacturer were analyzed for linear and volumetric wear using a co-ordinate measuring machine. The mated stem was a shorter 12/14, threaded trunnion (n=72) or a longer, smooth 11/13 trunnion (n=32). The abductor moment arm was calculated from pre-revision radiographs. Independent predictors of linear and volumetric wear included taper angle, stem type, and the horizontal moment arm. Tapers mated with the threaded 12/14 trunnion had significantly higher rates of volumetric wear (0.402 mm3/yr vs. 0.123 mm3/yr [t=-2.145, p=0.035]). There was a trend to larger abductor moment arms being protective (p=0.055). Design variation appears to play an important role in taper-trunnion junction failure. We recommend that surgeons bear these findings in mind when considering the use of a short, threaded trunnion with a cobalt-chromium head.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate whether design features of the taper-trunnion junction influence wear rates in large head metal-on-metal hip replacements.
summary_en.method: Linear and volumetric wear of tapers from 104 explanted hip replacements were measured using coordinate metrology, and correlated with design parameters and abductor moment arm from radiographs.
summary_en.result: Shorter, threaded 12/14 trunnions exhibited significantly higher volumetric wear rates than longer, smooth 11/13 trunnions.
summary_en.validation: Validation was carried out by coordinate measuring machine analysis of retrieved implants, though no controlled experimental validation was performed.
